paragraphs: Children in care in Burnley are looked after by Lancashire County Council's fostering service and by independent agencies, including those shown above. Burnley stands out in the council's own figures. Its agency foster care market position statement of April 2025 names Burnley, with Preston, West Lancashire and Lancaster, as the districts with the most requests for homes that are hard to find, and says these four accounted for 69% of its requests to agencies in 2024-25. More than half of all requests were for children over 11, and 14% were for brothers and sisters to live together.

The council has tried local ways of keeping carers going. It piloted fostering communities in Burnley, Pendle and the Ribble Valley, where very experienced carers give peer support to a small group of carers who have few family and friends nearby. It has also appealed for parent and child carers, who look after a parent and baby together, usually for around 12 weeks. Its informal 'talk to the team' drop-ins in East Lancashire have included one at Charter Walk shopping centre in Burnley in December 2026.

To foster for Lancashire you need to be over 21, with no upper age limit, and to live in or close to the county. You do not need to drive or to have formal qualifications. New carers complete the Skills to Foster course and join an induction academy and a mentoring scheme, with support available around the clock. The council says it has raised its allowances because of rising costs. It is also one of five councils behind Foster with us, the regional recruitment hub launched in July 2024.
If you live in Burnley, speak to the council and two or three of the agencies above, and ask each about support for older children, sibling groups and parent and child care.
